subject: SIG questionnaire: hosting deployment options and evidence plan (Acme Health)
messages:
From: Taylor Reed <taylor.reed@acmehealth.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Health Security <security@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-18 09:42 -0700
Subject: SIG questionnaire: hosting deployment options and evidence plan

Hi Markus,

Thanks for taking our SIG. We're working through the hosting section and need a succinct explanation of how Redwood's three hosting options (hosted, dedicated, private/VPC/on-prem) map to responsibility, evidence, and control locations. The reviewers want: a clear differentiation for (1) data in transit/at rest responsibility, (2) customer control over keys and logs, (3) infrastructure ownership, and (4) what concrete artifacts you can provide for each option (e.g., SOC2 scope statement, network diagrams, KMS integration notes, sample audit logs).

Can you send a short comparative brief plus a list of deliverables you can attach to the SIG? We're on a tight timeline for our security committee - ideally by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Taylor
Taylor Reed
Senior Security Analyst, Acme Health
security@acmehealth.com

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Taylor Reed <taylor.reed@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-18 11:05 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG questionnaire: hosting deployment options and evidence plan

Taylor — thanks for the clear ask. I've attached a short comparison matrix and a proposed evidence index that maps SIG sections to specific deliverables. High level summary below; full details are attached (redwood_deployment_comparison_v1.xlsx and sig-mapping-hosted-dedicated-private.pdf).

Quick comparative summary (1 paragraph each):
- Hosted (Redwood API): we operate the control plane and serving runtime in our multi-tenant hosted environment. Redwood manages keys for infrastructure; customers can bring their own keys for workspace-level encryption on request (enterprise only). Evidence we can supply: SOC 2 report covering hosted services, architecture diagram showing tenancy and network boundaries, sample redacted audit logs and token-level usage breakdown, and our data processing addendum.
- Dedicated (Reserved capacity): dedicated GPU pools logically isolated to the customer, deployed in our cloud tenancy. Customer data is isolated; keys may be customer-managed via KMS integration. Evidence: SOC 2 scope statement that includes dedicated instances, dedicated deployment diagram, KMS integration notes, and sample per-customer audit events.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): deployed into customer VPC or on-prem cluster; customer controls network, keys, and physical infrastructure. Redwood provides control-plane connectors and an evidence bundle (deployment runbook, installer hash, and guided audit checklist). Evidence: deployment checklists, installer signatures, and a customer-owned audit log configuration example.

Next step: Jasmine, Aditya — can you assemble the specific artifacts listed in the attached mapping? I propose we produce an "evidence index" CSV (attached) that points the SIG reviewer to the exact file for each question. Taylor — if you confirm this approach we'll aim to deliver the index and attachments tomorrow EOD.

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Product Security, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com

--
attachments: redwood_deployment_comparison_v1.xlsx (xlsx), sig-mapping-hosted-dedicated-private.pdf (pdf)

Markus — on it. I’ll own assembly of the artifacts and the SIG mapping. Plan and owners below:

2) Architecture diagrams — Aditya to update per-environment diagrams (hosted multi-tenant, dedicated pool, VPC connector) to show network boundaries and control plane flow (owner: Aditya).
3) KMS and keys — I’ll draft a one-page KMS integration summary showing which options support customer-managed keys and how keys are used (owner: Jasmine).
4) Audit logs & sample events — generate redacted sample audit lines for each env (owner: Aditya).
5) Installer signatures / runbooks (private) — assemble installer hash and runbook excerpt (owner: Jasmine + infra team).

Target: initial package (evidence-index CSV + PDFs) by 2027-05-19 17:00 PT. I’ll drop drafts to the security slack channel for quick review.

Jasmine Liu

Taylor — delivering the first package now. Files uploaded to the Drive link and attached below: evidence-index-20270520.csv (index), redwood_deployment_comparison_v1.xlsx (matrix), sig-mapping-hosted-dedicated-private.pdf (detailed mapping), sample-audit-lines.jsonl (redacted), hosted-arch-diagram.pdf, dedicated-arch-diagram.pdf, private-runbook-excerpt.pdf. The evidence index maps each SIG control to the file that answers or provides artifacts.

Short notes on tricky SIG sections:
- Data residency: hosted runs in regions we publish; for strict residency customers we recommend Dedicated or Private and we provide region pinning for Dedicated.
- Key custody: Hosted supports Redwood-managed keys by default; Dedicated supports BYOK via KMS integration; Private leaves key custody fully to the customer.
- Auditability: hosted offers redacted logs and usage exports; Dedicated includes per-customer audit streams; Private logs live in customer storage.

If you want us to attach statements to the questionnaire itself, we can draft concise answers for the SIG form fields and include links to specific pages in the index.

Markus
